name: Silver Star Mountain
blurb: The twin-summited granite peak east of Washington Pass, hiding a gentle glacier behind its cliffs.
permit: Northwest Forest Pass. No overnight permit is needed in the national forest. The North Cascades Highway closes for the winter.

routes.name: Silver Star Glacier
routes.summary: A climbers path up Silver Star Creek, a brushy climb toward Burgundy Col, then the Silver Star Glacier to the col between the twin summits and a short scramble east.
skills: Route finding through brush and boulders
Class 3 scrambling, with a low fifth-class step if you miss the ramp

line.source: Placed by hand on terrain data and published route descriptions; not surveyed

waypoints.name: Silver Star Creek
waypoints.note: Roadside parking where the highway crosses Silver Star Creek, east of Washington Pass.

waypoints.name: High camp
waypoints.note: Sandy and heather sites below Burgundy Col. Water from snowmelt.

sections.note: Climbers path up the east side of Silver Star Creek to an open basin.
Cross to the west side and climb steep brush, boulders and snow toward Burgundy Col, avoiding the gullies at the head of the basin.
Rising traverse south over a subsidiary ridge onto the Silver Star Glacier, then up to the col between the summits.
Scramble east to the higher summit. An easy ramp about 40 ft below the top avoids a short low fifth-class step.

pois.name: Burgundy Col
pois.note: Gap between Burgundy Spire and Silver Star; early-season parties sometimes rappel a short step nearby.
